name: GO Classes CS | C-Programming | Weekly Quiz 4

question.text:
What will be the output of the following C code?

#include<stdio.h>
void fun (char *p){
    p++[1]= 'E';
    ++*p++;
    printf("%c",*p);
}
int main(){
    char c[]= "IISc";
    fun(c);
}
  1. I
  2. S
  3. E
  4. c

Which of the following(s) function declarations can be used to pass the following array?

char myArray[3][4];

  1. void fun(char a[3][]);
  2. void fun(char a[][4]);
  3. void fun(char (*a)[4]);
  4. void fun(char **a);

What will be the output of the following program?

#include<stdio.h>
struct _myst{
    char b[20];
    char *a;
    struct _myst *c;
}x[2] = {"GATE", "Overflow", x+1, "GO", "Classes", x}, *p = x;
typedef struct _myst myst;

myst* mystry(myst *p, int n){
    if (n<=0) return p++;
    if(n%2) return mystry(p->c, n-2);
    else return mystry(p->c, n-1);
}
int main()
{
    printf("%s",mystry(p,2023)->a);
}
  1. GATE
  2. Overflow
  3. Run time error
  4. Compile-time error

Consider the following declaration of $a$.

int a[100][200][30];

What will be the integer value of $a[50][300] - a[10][500]?$

What will be the output of the following C program?

#include<stdio.h>
void main()
{
    int i=6;
    for(--i; --i; i--)
    {
      printf("%d",i);
    }
}
  1. $42$
  2. $31$
  3. Infinite loop
  4. None of these

Assume starting addresses of array arrop and twoD are $1000$ and $2000$ respectively. Also, assume that addresses are of $8$ bytes and integers are of $4$ bytes.

What will be the value of $\textsf{*pp[1]}$ after the last line $\textsf{(pp++)}$ of the following program?

int main()
{
    int **pp;
    int *arrop[3];
    int twoD[3][3] = {{1,2,3}, {7,8,9}, {4,5,6}};
    pp = arrop;
    arrop[0] = (int *)(twoD+2);
    arrop[1] = (int *)(twoD+1);
    arrop[2] = (int *)(twoD);
    pp++;
}

What will be the output of the following program?

struct s{
    int i;
    struct s *p;
};

struct s arr[4] = { 7, arr+3,
    8, arr+2,
    9, arr,
    10, arr+1,
};

struct s *ap[] = {arr+3, arr+2, arr+1, arr};
struct s **pp =ap;
int main()
{
    printf("%d", ap[pp[0]->p->i%2]->i++);
}
  1. $7$
  2. $10$
  3. $9$
  4. $8$

What will be the output of the following program ?

#include<stdio.h>
void fun(int c[2][2]){
    c = c+1;
    *c[1] = 5;
    (*c)[1] = 6;
}
int main()
{
    int a[3][2] = {{1,2}, {10,20}, {40, 50}};
    fun(a);
    printf("%d %d", a[2][0], a[1][0]);
}
  1. $5\; 10$
  2. $10\; 5$
  3. $10\; 40$
  4. Error since $c$ is a two-dimensional array, and we can not update the value of $c$ using $c=c+1.$

What will be the output if you compile and execute the following C code?

extern int x;
void main()
{
    printf("%d",x);
    x=2;
}
int x=23;
  1. $0$
  2. $2$
  3. $23$
  4. Compiler error

After executing following lines of C code, $\textsf{&arr[1][2]}$ is same as:

int (*a)[3];
int arr[2][3];
a = arr+1;

  1. &a[0][2]

  2. (*a+2)

  3. (int *)(&arr+1)-1

  4. *(a+2)

What will be printed by the following program?

#include<stdio.h> 
struct card
{
    int face ;
};
typedef struct card Card ;
Card c ;
void pass(Card c);
int main()
{
    c.face = 1;
    printf("%d ", c.face);
    pass(c);
    printf("%d",c.face);
}

void pass(Card c)
{
    c.face = 5;
    printf("%d ",c.face);
}
  1. $1\; 1\; 1$
  2. $1\; 5\; 1$
  3. $1\; 5\; 5$
  4. None of these

What will be the output of the following program?

int main()
{
    int arr[3][3] = {{1,2,3}, {4,5,6}, {7,8,9}};
    int *p;
    p = (int *)(arr+2);
    printf("%d", *(p-2));
}

What is the output of the following code?

#include<stdio.h>
int main() {
    unsigned int x = 1;
    int y = -2;
    (x + y > 0) ? printf("WRONG ANSWER") : printf("CORRECT ANSWER");
}
  1. WRONG ANSWER
  2. CORRECT ANSWER
  3. Prints nothing
  4. None of these

What will be the output of the following C program?

#include<stdio.h>
void main()
{
    int b=20, c=30;
    printf("%d%d\n", b<<2>>4, c<<2>>4);
}

Consider the following declaration of pointer variable p.

int (*p)[10];

If the initial value of $p$ is $1100,$ then what will be the value of $\textsf{p+1}?$

It is given that, system has $8$ bytes of address size and $4$ bytes of integer size.

  1. $1140$
  2. $1180$
  3. $1104$
  4. $1108$

void mystery(int n) {
  if (n <= 1) {
    printf("%d", n);
  }
  else {
    printf("%d, ", n);

    mystery(n/2);
    printf(", %d", n);
  }
}

What will be the output printed by $\text{mystery(12)}?$

  1. $12, 6, 3, 1, 3, 6, 12$
  2. $12, 6, 3, 1, 3, 6,$
  3. $12, 6, 3, 1, 3, 6, 12,$
  4. None of these

Assume that an int variable takes $4$ bytes and a char variable takes $1$ byte. What is the output of the code below?

int main()
{
    int arr[]={10,20,30,40,50,60};
    int *ptr1=arr;
    int *ptr2=arr+5;
    printf("Number of elements between two pointer are: %d.", 
    (ptr2 - ptr1));
    printf("Number of bytes between two pointer are: %d.", 
    (char*)ptr2 - (char*)ptr1);
}
  1. Number of elements between two pointer are: $5$. Number of bytes between two pointers are: $20$
  2. Number of elements between two pointer are: $20.$ Number of bytes between two pointers are: $20$
  3. Number of elements between two pointer are: $5.$ Number of bytes between two pointers are: $5$
  4. Compile time error

What will be the output of the following program?

main()
{
    int a[2][2] = { {1,2},{3,4} };
    int(*p)[2][2];
    p = &a;
    printf("%d", (*p)[0][0]);
}
  1. $1$
  2. $3$
  3. $4$
  4. None of these

What will be the output if we compile and execute the following C code?

#include<stdio.h>
void main(){
int i=10;
static int x=i;
if(x==i)
    printf("Equal");
else if(x>i)
    printf("Greater than");
else
    printf("Less than");
}
  1. Equal
  2. Greater than
  3. Less than
  4. Compiler error

Consider below two files p$1$.c and p$2$.c

We compile both files independently and link them in case the compilation is successful.

Which of the following(s) is/are TRUE?

  1. p$1$.c can not be compiled as there is no main function in the file.
  2. Line $3$ in p$1$.c will produce a compilation error because of the redefinition of variable $a.$
  3. Line $6$ in p$2$.c will produce a compilation error since the extern does not allocate memory to variables.
  4. Line $7$ in p$2$.c will produce a compilation error.
